name: Perihilar Cholangiocarcinoma

ethnicAssociations: Higher incidence in Southeast Asian populations

criteria.description: Imaging evidence of biliary ductal stricture at the hepatic hilum
Histopathological confirmation of adenocarcinoma from bile duct biopsy or brush cytology
Elevated serum CA 19-9 tumor marker above 100 U/mL

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of imaging evidence of biliary stricture at the hepatic hilum plus histopathological confirmation of adenocarcinoma
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis may be supported by elevated CA 19-9 and exclusion of benign causes of biliary obstruction

laboratory: Elevated serum bilirubin with predominant conjugated hyperbilirubinemia
Elevated alkaline phosphatase and gamma-glutamyl transferase (GGT)
imaging: MRI/MRCP showing biliary ductal stricture at the hepatic hilum
CT scan demonstrating mass lesion at bile duct confluence
Cholangiography revealing irregular narrowing or obstruction of the hepatic ducts
genetic: No specific germline mutations identified; somatic mutations in KRAS, TP53, and IDH1/2 may be present
other: Histopathology confirming adenocarcinoma with glandular differentiation
Endoscopic retrograde cholangiopancreatography (ERCP) with brush cytology

distinguishingFeatures: Lack of mass lesion on imaging
History of biliary surgery or trauma
Absence of malignant cells on biopsy
Mass centered in gallbladder rather than bile duct confluence

redFlags: Unexplained weight loss with biliary obstruction
Persistent elevation of CA 19-9 despite biliary drainage
references: Bridgewater J, Galle PR, Khan SA, et al. Guidelines for the diagnosis and management of intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma. J Hepatol. 2014;60(6):1268-1289.
Razumilava N, Gores GJ. Cholangiocarcinoma. Lancet. 2014;383(9935):2168-2179.
